questions.question: What does CCTV stand for? Explain briefly. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• CCTV stands for Closed-Circuit Television. It is a video surveillance system used to
  • monitor and record activities in a building. It consists of cameras, cables or network
  • connections, a monitor, and a recording device (DVR/NVR). It is used for security, safety,
  • and crime prevention. In Building Management System (BMS), CCTV helps monitor
  • entrances, exits, corridors, parking areas, and other important locations. [U][CO1]
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the advantages of TRIACs over mechanical relays. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• A TRIAC (Triode for Alternating Current) is a semiconductor switching device used to
  • control AC (alternating current) power. It acts like an electronically controlled switch,
  • allowing current to flow through a load in both directions when triggered. TRIACs have no
  • mechanical contacts, reducing wear and tear. They switch electrical loads faster than
  • mechanical relays. They operate without clicking or switching noise. They have a longer
  • operating life due to the absence of contact wear. They require less maintenance and are
  • suitable for frequent switching in building automation systems. [A][CO2]
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of IDS as a layer of physical security. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Intrusion Detection System is a system that detects unauthorized entry or suspicious activity
  • within a building and sends alerts to security personnel or a central monitoring system.
  • Detects unauthorized entry into buildings or restricted areas.
  • Uses door contacts, motion detectors, and glass-break sensors to detect intrusions.
  • Triggers alarms when suspicious activity or unauthorized access is detected.
  • Sends alerts to security personnel or the Building Management System (BMS).
  • Helps prevent theft, vandalism, and unauthorized access by enabling a quick response.
  • [A] [CO3]
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: How do controllers use VFDs to control pumps and fans? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Variable Frequency Drive is an electronic device used to control the speed of an AC
  • motor by varying the frequency and voltage of the electrical supply. Controllers use VFDs
  • to vary the motor speed by changing the supply frequency. Sensors measure parameters
  • such as pressure, temperature, and airflow. {Use feedback path to control}. The controller
  • automatically adjusts the VFD speed according to the required pressure, flow, or
  • temperature. VFDs reduce motor speed when full capacity is not required, saving energy.
  • By using VFDs they provide smooth starting and stopping, reduce mechanical stress, and
  • improve system efficiency. [U][CO1]
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the advantages and applications of DCV in modern buildings. / [CO2] [5x3 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• DCV stands for Demand-Controlled Ventilation. It is a ventilation control strategy that
  • automatically adjusts the amount of fresh outdoor air supplied to a building according to
  • actual occupancy and ventilation demand. DCV helps maintain indoor air quality while
  • reducing unnecessary ventilation, fan energy consumption, and heating or cooling loads.
  • Reduces energy consumption by supplying ventilation only when required. Uses CO₂
  • sensors to adjust fresh air supply according to occupancy there by ensuring improved air
  • quality. Reduces HVAC operating costs and electricity bills. Automatically adjusts
  • ventilation based on the number of people in a room {occupancy-based control}. Used in
  • offices, classrooms, shopping malls, conference rooms, and other modern buildings
  • through the Building Management System (BMS). [A][CO2]
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
